## Instructor

**Dr. Dunstan Matekenya**

Dr. Dunstan Matekenya is a Data Scientist at the World Bank Group with over 15 years of experience
applying data science to a wide range of development challenges. His work spans geospatial data,
mobile phone data, machine learning, artificial intelligence and official statistics, supporting
evidence-based decision making across multiple sectors and countries. More recently, his work has
focused on adapting and advancing AI technologies for low-resource African languages, including
leading initiatives in Malawi to develop automatic speech recognition (ASR) and machine translation
systems for Chichewa.

Teaching and capacity building are a central part of his work. He has extensive experience teaching
data science, machine learning and AI to public servants, researchers, students and practitioners
in Asia, through the UN Statistical Institute for Asia and the Pacific (SIAP), and across Africa,
including Malawi, Rwanda, Senegal, Cameroon and Tunisia. Before joining the World Bank, he was a
Statistician at the National Statistical Office of Malawi, where he contributed to major national
statistical programmes and led the Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Unit.

### Recent teaching

- **2025 · Rwanda:** Applied data analytics with Python for 60 public servants from institutions
  in Rwanda's National Statistical System, as part of the
  [Data Science Capacity Building Initiative (DSCBI)](https://dmatekenya.github.io/AIMS-DSCBI/)
  with AIMS.
- **2024 · Tunisia:** Generative AI course for participants from 12 African countries, part of the
  Data in Health project, a collaboration between the World Bank and the African Development Bank (AfDB).
- **2023 · Malawi:** Large language models (LLMs) course for ICT professionals.
- **2018–present:** *Big Data Analytics with Python* (this course), at SIAP (Japan) and AIMS
  (Rwanda, Senegal and Cameroon). See [Past iterations](#past-iterations).
